Subject: Re: Annual token commitments — initial ask

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. FastFin is evaluating annual commit options for our hosted usage starting January. A few priorities from our side: predictable unit economics for budgeting, the ability to absorb quarterly spikes with minimal penalty, and an option to roll unused commit forward or receive credits.

High level numbers from our finance team: we expect 90M–120M tokens/month average in year one with seasonal spikes up to ~220M. We are leaning toward an annual commit but want the math on at least two flavors — a firm slab (simple tiers) and a smoothing model (quarterly smoothing / roll-forward).

Can you share: 1) a short proposal that maps Starter/Growth/Enterprise slabs to per-token committed vs overage pricing, 2) details on how rollover/credits would work, and 3) any SLA tradeoffs by tier (latency, allocation guarantees, and priority capacity)?

Attaching a tiny sample of our monthly forecast for context (FastFin_Monthly_plan.xlsx).

Best,
Sarah
Director of Platform Engineering
FastFin

Sarah — great context, thanks. I put together a concise proposal below and attached a short slide deck that you can share with finance/legal. High level: we can offer both slab-based commits and a smoothing option that combines quarterly true-ups with rollover credits. I summarized trade-offs so you can pick what matters most.

Attached: Redwood_Commit_Slides.pdf (summary, numbers, and example math) and SLA_Appendix.docx (detailed SLOs by tier).

Proposal (annual commit flavors) — Starter / Growth / Enterprise
- Starter: 100M tokens/year commit (baseline) — committed price $0.00012 / token; overage $0.00016 / token. No capacity reservation; best-effort latency targets.
- Growth: 1.2B tokens/year commit (recommended for your stated volumes) — committed price $0.000095 / token; overage $0.00013 / token. Includes seasonal burst buffer up to +25% of monthly baseline with billed overage at committed rate for burst usage within buffer.
- Enterprise: 5B+ tokens/year commit — committed price tiered down to $0.00007 / token depending on final volume; overage $0.00010 / token. Includes reserved capacity pools and SLA credits for latency/availability breaches.

Smoothing / roll-forward options (optional add-on):
- Quarterly true-up: if a quarter is under-committed, we grant a credit equal to 50% of the value of unused tokens that can be applied to future quarters in the same contract year.
- Full-year reconciliation: any remaining unused commit at year-end can be converted to a one-time credit at 40% of committed value or rolled into the next year at a 20% discount to list committed price (customer choice at renewal).

SLA trade-offs:
- Starter: 99.5% platform availability SLA; best-effort burst handling
- Growth: 99.9% SLA; prioritization on routing during regional pressure; access to dedicated short-term burst capacity for planned events (requires 48h notice)
- Enterprise: 99.95% SLA; reserved pools, onboarding assistance, quarterly performance reviews, and a response SLT for incidents

Quick notes:
- We also offer a one-time onboarding credit and professional services rates for integration/ops work; can be used to offset early underutilization.
- For contract/legal we typically attach the SLA_Appendix and an implementation MOP.

Next steps: if Growth looks closest to what you want, I can send a formal commercial term sheet with example monthly invoices and an MAP (mutual action plan) to show timelines for billing, kickoff, and capacity ramp.

Thanks — copying Marissa for pricing/legal escalation if needed.

— Priyom

Priyom / Sarah — looping in Ben for legal/pricing ops. Priyom, recommended commercial play: offer Growth slab with these practical concessions to close in this quarter: 

- Commit: 1.2B tokens/yr at the Growth committed rate ($0.000095)
- Burst buffer: allow +25% buffer for up to two distinct months per contract year (explicitly for seasonality) — beyond that buffer, overage billing applies at the Growth overage rate.
- Onboarding credit: one-time $15k credit applied against the first two invoices (we can flex to $20k if they sign within the procurement window).
- Quarterly smoothing: quarterly true-up with 60% credit conversion of unused tokens (more generous than our standard 50% to help them ramp).

Ben — please verify in the contract if we can escalate the true-up to 60% and confirm DocuSign flow. If legal is good, Priyom I recommend sending a short commercial term sheet + MAP and include the DocuSign link for a 30-day signature target.

Sarah — happy to jump on a quick 20-minute call to walk finance through the sample invoice and MAP.
